annotations.text:
One direction per row: the base rendering at the left, its variants to the right (A' = A with C's For-you box, C' = C after the clicks, E'…J' = the question-centred versions).

Same reply everywhere. The model writes the substance (markers, verdict, one decision with its default); a function-hooks mod draws the form.

All boards are 520 px wide: the transcript column of a Claude Desktop window at ~40% of the screen.

A · Markers kept
Why: zero learning curve, your six emoji stay in the raw transcript, works on Desktop as markdown fallback.
Trade-off: emoji carry the colour, so at a glance six markers in a mono font look alike; emoji widths shift alignment in some terminals.

B · Colour gutter, no emoji
Why: colour reads faster than a glyph; the label column (DECIDE / DONE / READ / NOTE / SKIP) is searchable and aligns perfectly in monospace.
Trade-off: the mod strips the emoji from the display, so a reader without the mod sees the raw markers; colour-blind readers rely on the labels only.

C · Headline + drawers (my candidate)
Why: the least to read. One inverse-video headline, the decision box, then drawers: READ always open, DONE / NOTES / SKIP folded with counts. Narration between tool calls folds too.
Trade-off: the proofs behind each done task are one click away, not on screen; clicks need the fullscreen renderer, keyboard otherwise.

D · Dashboard
Why: proof gets its own column, so 'verified' is visible per task; counters on top; scan by column like a CI summary.
Trade-off: needs a wide pane (≥100 columns); the model must write each done line as 'task — proof' for the mod to split it; dense for a short reply.

Round 2: six more, each on a different axis — background colour, one-colour ASCII, who-acts lanes, sticky board, emoji as icons, time rail.

Right column: the same direction rebuilt around the question — options with consequence, time and risk, a recommended tag, a visible default with its countdown, hotkeys 1·2·3, and an 'other' field.

All boards are 520 px wide: the transcript column of a Claude Desktop window at ~40% of the screen. Two-lane layouts stack; three-column boards get tight on purpose, so you can judge them at that width.

Animations are CSS here; in the terminal the mod redraws at ≤10 fps, so pulses and blinks are the realistic ceiling.

E · Tinted rows
Why: the background carries the marker for what needs you (decide, read) and the eye sorts rows by tint before reading a word. Done rows are neutral with a dark-green check, so green never floods the card (changed on request: the green fills added too much colour).
Trade-off: tints must stay legible on both terminal themes; the decision row pulses.

E′ · Tinted rows, asking
The question owns the card: recommended option as the bright row, default option marked and timed with a shrinking bar, third row is a free-text field. Rest of the card folded to one line.

F · Receipt
Why: one colour, ASCII only, works in every terminal ever made and in a screen reader; dotted leaders line the statuses up in a column.
Trade-off: no colour semantics at all — [OK] [!!] [??] carry everything; retro look is a taste.

F′ · Receipt, asking
The question as a till menu: numbered items, TIME and RISK columns, the house recommendation starred, default and countdown in the header, 'press 1-3 then Enter'.

G · Two lanes
Why: the split is semantic, not cosmetic — left is what needs you (decide, read, blocked), right is what I did. You can read only the left lane and lose nothing you must act on.
Trade-off: needs ≥100 columns; bubbles cost vertical space.

G′ · Two lanes, asking
Left: the options as quick-reply bubbles with hotkeys. Right: for each option, a preview bubble of what happens next, plus the 'why I recommend' bubble. Like a chat with quick replies.

H · Sticky-note board
Why: three columns by what you do with it (decide / done / read), one note per fact, paper backgrounds; notes drop in.
Trade-off: the busiest of the ten; small type; needs a wide pane. Best for long replies, worst for a one-liner.

H′ · Board, asking
Options are notes you drag into DECIDED (or press 1·2·3); each note carries effort dots and a risk stripe; the default slides in by itself when the countdown ends; a WHY column explains the ask.

I · Big emoji sections
Why: your markers become section icons, 40px tall, with a coloured left border and a soft gradient per section — the emoji finally carry weight instead of hiding in the gutter.
Trade-off: emoji rendering differs per terminal font; gradients are Desktop-only (terminal falls back to flat tints).

I′ · Emoji tiles, asking
Three big tiles, one per option, the recommended one glowing; consequence, time and risk under each; default with countdown; an 'other' field in the third tile.

J · Timeline rail
Why: the reply is a story in time — each done task is a node with its minute, the warning hangs off the node it belongs to, the decision is the pulsing 'now' node, the next step is a dashed ghost.
Trade-off: order is not always the point; timestamps cost 6 columns; a reply with ten tasks becomes a long rail.

J′ · Branching futures, asking
From the 'now' node, three branches to three futures: what the rail looks like at 11:50 if you say yes, where it ends if you say no, and a stretch you write yourself. Recommended branch solid and animated, others dashed.

K · gmorel-1.0.0 — your layout (final render only, notes live here)
Top to bottom: header "For you" (a dim green ✓ at its right when an observer agent is running) · four counters from D: decision · done, proven · to read · blocked · the decision box from C: yellow border, DECISION label, default spelled out, question in bold, two labelled buttons · the marker lines of A with their emoji (🟢 done with proof, ⚠️ read, ▫️ notes) · one dim line for the ℹ️ skippable items with [ show ].
Fourth theme of the repo: hooks/themes/gmorel.ts, 1.0.0, transcribed from this artboard.

C′ · after the clicks
Asked on the canvas: C, once the buttons have been pressed. [yes, patch it] turns the decision box green and puts the answer in the prompt box ($.prompt.fill) — Enter sends it, Esc puts the question back; nothing is sent behind your back. [open] on DONE and NOTES unfolds them in place and the button becomes [close]. [show] on the folded narration reveals the two tool calls and the narration line, dim and italic. SKIP was not touched, so it stays folded.
Every state change is one $.ui.invalidate redraw, so no frame animates; the only motion is the cursor.

K′ · gmorel-1.0.0 in a real transcript — final render only, explanations here
Top to bottom: 1 your prompt · 2 a background-task notification folded to one dim line with [show] · 3 a canvas comment arriving as a compact cyan card: artifact name, anchored artboard, time, the quoted text only, short thread id, a link to open it on the canvas — the boilerplate of the raw message is hidden · 4 the tool calls of the turn folded to one dim line · 5 the K card: header with the dim ✓ (an observer was running), four counters, the decision box with its buttons, the marker lines, the ℹ️ fold · 6 the outgoing side, a green card: the reply Claude posted in the same thread, the thread's resolved state, time, links to the full reply and to reopen · 7 the turn footer and the prompt box.
Mechanism: 3 is a UserMessage whose text starts with "[Artifact comment sent to Claude]" (parsed for artifact, thread, quoted lines); 6 pairs the Artifact tool calls reply/resolve carrying the same thread id.
Check: is this enough to implement? Anything missing goes in a comment on this artboard.

K″ · the decision box grows into a chooser
A 🟡 with 2–4 options is drawn as numbered rows inside the yellow box: title, badge (recommended / default), one line of consequence, and a right column with the estimate, the risk (green / amber / red) and the theoretical cost. The default and its timer come from the "if you say nothing" clause. Row 1 tinted because it is recommended. Keys 1–4 fill the prompt; Enter sends. The rest of the card folds to one line so the question owns the screen.

K · blocked
A 🔴 replaces the yellow box with a red one: what is blocked, what only you can do, the command to run, what continues meanwhile. The blocked counter turns red; the decision counter goes dim at 0. Done rows keep their proofs.

K · an answer
No 🟡, no 🔴, no 🟢: the header says Answer · nothing to do, the counters grid is dropped, no witness ✓ is claimed.
Scan order by colour: the verdict sits in a cyan-edged box, its key words coloured (green = what holds, amber = the limit); context lines open with a bold white lead and step back to grey; identifiers are chips; table labels are coloured by meaning (green shown · grey absent · amber hidden); code output is grey, the command cyan; the picture line is italic.
Rule of the theme: white and bold only for what to read first — everything else steps back to grey.

K · long report
Eight 🟢 with their proofs and clickable paths, a code block with the test output, two ⚠️, one ▫️. The card scrolls with the transcript; nothing is truncated, the ℹ️ fold is the only hidden part. The tool calls of the turn fold to one line with a show chip.

K · one line
A reply that is a single 🟢 has no header and no counters: one bordered row with the marker, the text and the witness ✓. The background-task notification folds to one dim line with a show chip; the follow-up is again one row. The theoretical cost sits at the right of every footer.
